SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

enjoy verb

have the benefit of: good health, a right

also enjoy good health, enjoy a right, enjoy a good reputation, have the benefit of

classical

Caes. BC 3.49.2: ūtī autem ipsōs valētūdine nōn bonā
Traupman 61, 63, 310

ūtor, ūtī, ūsus sum

verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative

have, enjoy (health, good weather, a friendship, an office)

Lewis & Short: “to experience, undergo, receive, enjoy”: valētūdine bonā ūtī, to enjoy good health (Traupman 61); amplissimīs honōribus ūtī, to have held the highest offices (Cic. Fl. 45, Lewis & Short). The same verb is “use”.

Other words

  • fruor, fruī, frūctus sum — enjoy (a good one has: peace, liberty, life)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent, with the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: commoda quibus ūtimur lūcemque quā fruimur (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Mīrum est, nam valētūdine bonā ūteris.

    That’s strange, since you enjoy good health.Traupman 61

  • suum cuique per mē ūtī atque fruī licet

    as far as I am concerned, everyone may have and enjoy what is hisGell. 13.24.1

See also enjoy.

SourcesLewis & Short: utor · Lewis & Short: fruor
